items.title: Law firms weigh new capital models that preserve independence, reports ALM
items.summary: Law.com examines how private equity is approaching the legal sector, with growing interest in structures that provide capital without requiring wholesale operational change. Among the models discussed is a “managed services organization” (MSO) approach, which allows firms to access external funding while maintaining control over day-to-day practice. Learn more.

items.title: Maximizing IP portfolio value in Europe’s new patent era
items.summary: Europe’s new patent system is transforming enforcement—unlocking greater IP value and driving smarter licensing and monetization strategies. Click to learn more.

items.title: Opening arguments: Legal finance enters South Korea
items.summary: South Korea enters a new era of legal finance as cross-border disputes grow and arbitration reforms drive adoption among corporates and law firms. Read more.

items.title: SIAC: Caseload trends and the early engagement of third-party capital
items.summary: Legal finance is reshaping dispute strategy across Asia, with early-stage enforcement analysis, cross-border complexity and SIAC data revealing how claims are assessed, structured and pursued for recovery.

items.title: Bilanz reports on the rapid global growth of legal finance and its evolution into a corporate finance tool
items.summary: Managing Director Jörn Eschment discusses in Bilanz the rapid global growth of legal finance and its evolution into a corporate finance tool, with a focus on Switzerland and the broader European markets. Eschment, based in Switzerland, highlights how companies are using legal finance to monetize claims, manage litigation risk and reduce balance sheet volatility as demand accelerates worldwide. Learn more.

items.title: Original Jurisdiction reports on traditionally defense-focused Big Law firms entering plaintiff-side litigation
items.summary: David Lat, author of Original Jurisdiction, reports that traditionally defense-focused Big Law firms are increasingly representing corporate clients as plaintiffs. Driven by client demand and supported by legal finance, firms are taking on high-value affirmative matters using more flexible fee structures, allowing them to compete for plaintiff-side work while managing risk and preserving their core economic model. The article features perspectives from Burford’s Evan Meyerson and Vanessa Biondo. Learn more.

items.title: Where capital retreats, insolvency and restructuring claims step forward
items.summary: Ahead of INSOL London, corporates and restructuring professionals face shared pressures including rising costs, tightening liquidity and constrained financing. Learn more.

items.title: ALM examines alternative investment models in Big Law
items.summary: ALM reports on growing interest in minority investment structures for law firms in the U.S. and U.K., as traditional private equity approaches face structural challenges in partnership-based firms. Chief Development Officer Travis Lenkner describes a model centered on long-term capital, where investors participate through profit distributions, aligning more closely with law firm economics and governance.

items.title: Aviva Will appears on The Hub and Spoke podcast
items.summary: On The Hub and Spoke podcast, Vice Chair Aviva Will discusses what it takes to build a successful affirmative litigation program. The conversation covers four foundational pillars, alongside changes in the legal finance market and how companies are rethinking the role of litigation. Learn more.

items.title: Los Angeles Times reports that mid-market firms explore new funding paths to compete and scale
items.summary: Business by LA Times Studio, The Los Angeles Times' business magazine reports that mid-sized law firms are increasingly turning to outside capital to compete, recruit and retain talent, invest in technology and support growth.
